findings.rule: D37 (one entry group per sentence) / Constitution I.1; new path in this delta
findings.trigger: A cited resume-section skill gets group undefined, and the check treats undefined as a member of every group. A skill name therefore joins any entry's sentence. 'Data Analyst at Initech with SQL.' citing EXP-01 and skill:SQL passes, and so do 'Cleaned weekly sales data with SQL.' (EXP-01-1+skill:SQL) and 'Data analyst with SQL.' (SUM-01+skill:SQL). On the normal set, '<title> at <org> with <skill not in that entry>' citing [entry, skill:X] passes 582/582 (normal-001: 'QA Engineer at Tarang Foods with Kubernetes.'). 'Title at Org with MH1 and MH2' citing skill ids passes 100/100. Before this delta, skill ids supplied no words, so this path did not exist. The new prompt text invites the model to cite skill ids, so the D37 protection holds only for tools that sit in another entry's bullets. Candidate fix tested on the copy: give skill sets their own group (entryOf.get(id) ?? "skills"). A skills-only sentence still passes ('Excel, SQL.' 100/100 on the normal set, and the new test). A skill mixed with an entry or the summary in one sentence becomes null: 582/582 rejected, and 'Title at Org with MH1 and MH2' citing skill ids drops to 0/100. All positives in the test file and in my case list are kept.
findings.title: A resume skill id joins any entry group, so the employer-tool recombination D37 closed passes again via skill ids
findings.proof: Summary 'Data Analyst at Initech with SQL.' citing EXP-01 and skill:SQL (SQL in skills, in no Initech bullet), verifier supported for all; expect result.summary null.

findings.trigger: sentenceBreak splits at every . ! ? that is not followed by a digit, including periods inside names. A tool clause after an abbreviated organization therefore becomes its own sentence and may rest on any group. With each organization suffixed 'Pvt. Ltd.' (common in Indian resumes; the normal set has no dotted organization), 'QA Engineer at Tarang Foods Pvt. Ltd. with Node.js.' citing EXP-01 and PRJ-01-1 passes. The same template passes 336/336, against 0/336 without the suffix. 'Data Analyst at Initech with .NET.' (EXP-01 + another entry's .NET bullet) and 'Engineer at Yahoo! with Kotlin.' (EXP-02+PRJ-01-1) also pass. Candidate fix tested on the copy: /[.!?](?=\s+\p{Lu}|\s*$)/u, which splits only before whitespace and a capital letter or at the end. It rejects all three cases and the 336, and keeps every positive. The cost is 2/100 on 'Title at Org. mh1, mh2.' when a skill name starts lowercase (greytHR, dbt); those become null, which is safe.
findings.title: A period or bang inside a name ends the sentence, so a tool from another entry attaches to an abbreviated employer
findings.proof: Profile with EXP-01 organization 'Initech Pvt. Ltd.'; summary 'Data Analyst at Initech Pvt. Ltd. with Kotlin.' citing EXP-01 and PRJ-01-1, verifier supported for all; expect result.summary null.
